title: A gaze control of socially interactive robots in multiple-person interaction | Robotica

fields.value: Experimental technical/system study with performance evaluation of a proposed gaze-control model.

quotes.text: Interaction experiments with performance evaluation are given to verify that the proposed model is suitable to assess intended behaviors of individuals and perform gaze behavior about multiple persons.
A series of experiments were designed to show how much the gaze control model with perception modules works in the interaction situation with multiple people.

fields.value: Social gaze control for selecting an interaction partner or interlocutor in multiparty interaction; gaze is also framed as a signal of conversational attention.

quotes.text: In particular, as one of the most salient signals in human–robot interaction (HRI), robot gaze can be an excellent predictor of conversational attention and support communicative mechanisms such as turn-taking, synchronized speech, and suitable engagement actions.
Main interest of this paper is to propose a reliable gaze control model that performs gaze behavior effectively in the social interaction with multiple persons.

In order to face this issue, this paper examines social gaze behavior of the robot in the MPIs by incorporating of multimodal perceptual features from the interaction design with gaze control criteria.

fields.value: The paper does not provide a formal definition of robotic gaze, robotic attention, or gaze-based attention; it describes robot gaze as a predictor of conversational attention and defines its proposed system’s purpose as selecting a suitable interlocutor.

quotes.text: This paper proposes a computational model for selecting a suitable interlocutor of socially interactive robots in a situation interacting with multiple persons.
In particular, as one of the most salient signals in human–robot interaction (HRI), robot gaze can be an excellent predictor of conversational attention

fields.value: Gaze selects and visibly directs attention to an interlocutor based on interaction intent, supports engagement and attentive listening, and may support communicative mechanisms such as turn-taking.

quotes.text: In this regard, the robot easily identify the person who displays the greatest level of interaction intent by conducting socially acceptable decision-making and explicitly express attention to the designated target in a given situation by gaze control.

To achieve attentive listening by gaze control, the factor of communicative intimacy was configured to depend on the number of interlocutors’ responses, which indicate liking and disliking by providing relational questions.

fields.value: An autonomous, multimodal system extracts behavioral cues, applies temporal confidence reasoning and weighted feature scoring, combines this with physical-space and communicative-intimacy factors, and directs the robot’s gaze to the highest-scoring participant. The robot uses pre-scripted dialogue; the paper does not report Wizard-of-Oz control.

quotes.text: Each feature represents the perceptual information extracted by the multiple sensors of visual, auditory, and spatial modality, and a quantitative appraisal for each feature is used to the foundation for performing a gaze control of the robot targeted at multiple people.

fields.value: MERO is a stationary robotic head with a webcam, four microphones, a Kinect sensor, a 4-DOF neck, and 17-DOF face modules for eyebrows, eyelids, pupils, and lips.

quotes.text: As a stationary robotic head type, MERO is mainly designed by product designers based on what a sample target group of people perceived to be an aesthetically pleasing, human-friendly external appearance.

A webcam on the robot head, four microphones on the base, and a Kinect sensor located at a certain distance from the robot along the Z-axis are attached on the robot system in order to have a reliable perception
the robot is equipped to perform human tracking, shifts in gaze, head gestures, and facial expressions through 4-DOF neck and 17-DOF face modules (eyebrow, eyelid, pupil, and lip).

fields.value: The paper presents and evaluates a stationary robotic head that selects whom to look at in multiparty interaction using visual, auditory, and spatial cues, along with physical distance and conversational intimacy. It reports 93.3% success in a three-person scenario and 85.6% average agreement with participants’ target evaluations; the paper does not report a specific effect of the robot’s embodiment on these results.

RQ1; RQ2; RQ3; RQ4; RQ5 — The paper frames robotic gaze as conversational attention and partner selection, describes its role and reported performance in multiparty interaction, details the sensing and decision model, and identifies the MERO robot embodiment. It does not explain how embodiment influenced the study.
